children: Average daily cash market turnover on Indian stock exchanges climbed to a six-month high of ₹1.43 lakh crore in November, up from ₹1.24 lakh crore in October, as foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) returned aggressively to domestic equities, boosting trading activity.
Before November, the highest average daily turnover was recorded in May 2026, at ₹1.52 lakh crore, according to data compiled from the exchanges.

The pickup in trading activity coincided with a sharp recovery in benchmark indices. The Nifty 50 rallied more than 11% in November, marking its biggest monthly gain since November 2020, as foreign investors stepped up purchases following an extended period of selling.

FPIs have extended their buying streak to 19 consecutive trading sessions. With their purchase of $176 million on Friday, net FPI buying in November crossed the $16 billion mark, signalling a significant reversal in foreign investor sentiment towards Indian equities. The cumulative buying also marks the highest-ever FPI investment over such a short period.

The return of foreign capital has helped improve liquidity in the cash market. Increased institutional participation, coupled with the sharp market rebound, has encouraged investors to step up trading activity, particularly in stocks that had witnessed corrections in the preceding months.
Importantly, the increase in turnover has been accompanied by an improvement in delivery-based activity, suggesting that the rise is not entirely driven by short-term trading.

The average delivery volume as a proportion of total traded volume increased to 42% in November, compared with 39% in October. A higher delivery ratio indicates that a larger proportion of trades resulted in the actual transfer of shares, although it does not necessarily distinguish between fresh investments and investors exiting existing positions.

Meanwhile, brokerages remain constructive on the outlook for Indian equities, citing improving corporate profitability, easing oil prices, resilient consumer demand, strong domestic credit growth and a broadening private capital expenditure cycle as key supporting factors.
JPMorgan has set an end-2027 base-case target of 29,000 for the Nifty 50, factoring in modest valuation de-rating.

“Our end-2027 base-case target for the Nifty 50 is 29,000, which factors in modest valuation de-rating. We continue to favour domestic cyclicals over exporters, with a preference for quality and momentum stocks, particularly those demonstrating strong earnings momentum, while remaining underweight on value stocks,” said Rajiv Batra, head of Asia and co-head of global emerging markets equity strategy at JPMorgan.

However, Batra cautioned that elevated valuations, domestic policy headwinds and global uncertainties could limit further gains, reinforcing the need for a selective, disciplined and risk-aware investment approach.

title: Indian equity turnover hits six-month high as FPIs pump in $16 billion in November
